narrative:
The model determined that you have a 25% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this decision were the length of the loan you requested, the purpose of the loan, and the status of your checking account. Your short nine-month repayment period was the most influential factor and worked in your favor, as it is well below the 19-month average seen among approved applicants. The business purpose of your loan was the second most important factor and unfortunately pushed the prediction toward higher risk, since business loans are relatively uncommon among successful applications. Your checking account balance between 0 and 200 DM was the third strongest driver and also increased your risk score, because most approved applicants either have no checking account or maintain higher balances.

In short, although your short loan duration helped your case, the combination of a business purpose and a modest checking account balance outweighed that positive signal.

You should consider reapplying with a different loan purpose, such as home-related expenses, or explore building a stronger checking account balance before submitting a new request. Reviewing your overall credit history with a financial advisor may also help strengthen future applications. (218 words)
